draft.title: The spark in 1914
card: On 28 June 1914, Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, was shot dead in Sarajevo. The killer, Gavrilo Princip, was a young Bosnian Serb who wanted Bosnian Serbs freed from Austria-Hungary.
Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia for the killing. In late July it declared war on Serbia.
Europe's great powers were tied together by alliances, which were promises to help partners in a war. Russia backed Serbia, and Germany backed Austria-Hungary.
Declarations of war followed one after another. Germany and Russia were at war, then Germany and France. When Germany invaded Belgium, Britain declared war on 4 August 1914.
draft.remember: One killing was the spark, and the alliances turned a local crisis into a wider war.

a.q: Why did the killing in Sarajevo lead to a war across Europe?
opts: Alliances drew the great powers in one after another
Every European country had already planned to invade
Britain ordered the other powers to take sides at once
Serbia declared war on all the great powers in turn
a.why: Each power had promised to back a partner, so a war between two countries spread as others joined. The killing did not mean every country had planned to fight, and Serbia did not declare war on the great powers.
a.clue: Think about the promises between the great powers.

b.q: Which statement best describes the part played by the killing of Franz Ferdinand in 1914?
opts: It was the spark that set off a crisis already tense
It was the only cause of tension between the powers
It was a plan by Germany to start a war with Britain
It was the event that created the alliances in Europe
b.why: The killing set off a chain of war declarations in a Europe where the powers were already bound by alliances. It was not the only cause, because the alliances were already in place and the powers were already tense. It was also not a German plan to fight Britain.
b.clue: The alliances already existed before the shooting.

a.best: Alliances drew the great powers in one after another

b.best: It was the spark that set off a crisis already tense
